terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, transitive; with nē or ut + subjunctive
terms.comment: To warn and to advise alike: moneō nē, “I warn you not to”; moneō ut, “I advise you to”.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 1.23: mē, ut magnopere cavērem, praemonēbat (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Chiefly “remind” (of what is past, Lewis & Short), but also “warn, urge”.

phrases.latin: īnstruit et nātum ‘mediō’que ‘ut līmite currās, Īcare,’ ait ‘moneō, nē, sī dēmissior ībis, unda gravet pennās, sī celsior, ignis adūrat’
phrases.english: he instructs his son too: ‘I warn you, Icarus, keep to the middle course, so that the sea does not weigh down your wings if you go too low, nor the sun scorch them if you go too high’

phrases.latin: nam et monendī amīcī saepe sunt et objūrgandī
phrases.english: for friends must often be warned and scolded

sources: Lewis & Short: moneo · Lewis & Short: praemoneo · Lewis & Short: admoneo
